Q: How can I efficiently handle multi-tenant database connections in ASP.NET Core using SQL Server? A:

All of the above. It depends. Really. Except Dynamic connection strings per request which isn't a separate option. You're not asking about connections but multi-tenant database strategies. A connection object is always short lived.

Different applications will use different multi-tenancy strategies, depending on their requirements. Using a discriminator column like a TenantID may be enough for a school system, but a financial application would probably require separate databases.

Manageability requirements can also affect multi-tenancy decisions. Do you want to offer different backup/recovery plans per tenant or not? If you do, you probably need multiple databases.

EF Core's Multi-tenancy docs describe some of the options :

  • Discriminator column. Works but you'd need a way to filter all queries by that TenantID. If you forget that, you have a leak. EF Core handles this through global query filters. You'll have to filter any direct queries yourself. No way to offer individual backup/restores (unless you use partitioning). Performance could be an issue, eg one big tenant's data can result in inefficient query plans for smaller tenants. Blocking between tenants could be an issue, as they'd be using and locking the same tables.
  • Database per tenant. Maximum separation. All you need is a separate connection string per tenant. Maybe more costly in terms of maintenance but does allow you to offer different backup plans. No blocking between tenants either.
  • Schema per tenant. Still one database but if combined with different user accounts that only have access to their own schema, it can be very secure.

On top of them you could add using different tables per tenant, or accessing the data only through views that filter per tenant. You can use row-level security to control what each tenant sees.

There are database features that can help in each case. You can use table partitioning per TenantID for example, to store each tenant's data in a separate file, using its own partitioned indexes unaffected by other tenants. That would allow you to backup/restore the tenant's files instead of the entire database.

Q: Is it possible to run Change Data Capture without using the SQL Agent? A:

If the goal is to use a different mechanism than SQL Server Agent for scheduling execution of stored procedures there is possibility to achieve similar effect by using SQL Server Service Broker.

Related: Scheduled run of stored procedure on SQL server

Idea (simplified):

  1. Write a stored procedure/trigger that begins a conversation (BEGIN DIALOG) as loopback (FROM my_service TO my_service) - get conversation handler

    DECLARE @dialog UNIQUEIDENTIFIER;

BEGIN DIALOG CONVERSATION @dialog
       FROM SERVICE   [name] 
       TO SERVICE      'name' 
       ...;

  2. Start the conversation timer

    DECLARE @time INT;
BEGIN CONVERSATION TIMER (@dialog)     TIMEOUT = @time;

  3. After specified number of seconds a message will be sent to a service. It will be enqueued with associated queue.

    CREATE QUEUE queue_name WITH STATUS = ON, RETENTION = OFF
             , ACTIVATION (STATUS = ON, PROCEDURE_NAME = <procedure_name>
             , MAX_QUEUE_READERS = 20, EXECUTE AS N'dbo')
              , POISON_MESSAGE_HANDLING (STATUS = ON)

  4. Procedure will execute specific code and re-enable timer to fire again.

Q: How to do case insensitive search in Vim A:

By default, all searches in vi are case-sensitive. To do a case-insensitive search, go into command mode (press Escape), and type-
:set ignorecase
You can also type - :set ic as an abbreviation.

To change back to case-sensitive mode, type-
:set noignorecase or :set noic in command mode

Q: Can multiprocessing pool's workers start working immediately? A:

You haven't enlightened us with your Python code. You can arrange for processes to start (almost) immediately in various ways. This is probably the simplest...

from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
import time

def process(message: str) -> None:
    print(message)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    with ProcessPoolExecutor() as ppe:
        for _ in range(5):
            ppe.submit(process, "Running")
            time.sleep(2)

If you run this, you will note that "Running" appears at ~2 second intervals thereby demonstrating the virtual immediacy of the submission of the task to the process pool.

Q: How to make mysql2 gem to use new client version? A:

mysql2 is warning about the client library it was compiled against, not the actual database server version.

Your mysql --version output only shows the CLI/client executable version:

mysql  Ver 15.1 Distrib 10.5.29-MariaDB

but the mysql2 native extension is probably still linked against an old libmysqlclient (5.5.62).

You can verify that with:

ldd $(bundle show mysql2)/lib/mysql2/mysql2.so

On older upgraded systems it's common to have a newer MariaDB installation while Ruby gems still link against an older MySQL client library.

Usually reinstalling the gem against the current MariaDB dev package fixes it:

sudo apt install libmariadb-dev libmariadb-dev-compat

gem uninstall mysql2

bundle config build.mysql2 --with-mysql-config=/usr/bin/mariadb_config
bundle install

or:

gem install mysql2 -- --with-mysql-config=/usr/bin/mariadb_config

Q: Why is my SIMD implementation of octal string parsing unable to beat the compiler's? A:

You named your functions like parseOctalToBase10, however there is no conversion to decimal. You could consider it a conversion to binary as that's what the machine uses to represent numbers internally. Or like atoi just say it converts to a number / an integer.
